hypotheses.justification: The statement only needs `[Field E]` to elaborate: `InfinitePlace E` (def in InfinitePlace/Basic.lean, variable `[Field K]` only) and `InfinitePlace.comap` require just a field. The proof `InfinitePlace.comap_surjective` (Ramification.lean) needs only `[Algebra E K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic E K]`. That instance can be obtained without `NumberField E`: since `algebraMap E K` is injective (E is a field) and K has CharZero (from `NumberField K`), `RingHom.charZero (algebraMap E K)` (Algebra/Ring/CharZero.lean) gives `CharZero E`, hence `Algebra ℚ E` via `DivisionRing.toRatAlgebra`; the instance `IsScalarTower.rat` (Algebra/Module/Rat.lean) gives `IsScalarTower ℚ E K`; `NumberField K` gives `Algebra.IsAlgebraic ℚ K`, and `Algebra.IsAlgebraic.tower_top E` (RingTheory/Algebraic/Basic.lean) yields `Algebra.IsAlgebraic E K`. Then `InfinitePlace.comap_surjective v` closes the goal. Mathematically E embeds in the number field K, so it is automatically a subfield of a finite extension of ℚ; no degenerate case arises. (`[NumberField K]` is genuinely needed: for a huge transcendental K there are no complex embeddings, so `InfinitePlace K` is empty.)
